correctness.rationale: All hypotheses, normalization, domains and strictness boundaries are explicit. Differentiation gives the optimized action gap beta*lambda/(beta+lambda)*(neighbor_mean-theta), and the twin-row identity rules out differing actions within each block. The invertible block opinion system yields the four explicit patterns and exact interval endpoints; if a singleton is present, polarization is impossible, and two two-person communities have coincident intervals, proving sharp n=5. Exact rational checker verify.py independently enumerated 92,736 action profiles in 2,160 model cases; the all-size proof is analytical, not inferred from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The initiating 2026 paper establishes best responses and consensus conditions but not the mixed-action census. The closest balanced exact phase diagram permits only 1,2,4 equilibria, assuming equal block sizes and identical within-block fractions; its result does not imply a three-equilibrium outcome or a sharp five-person minimum. The new imbalance shifts the two polarization intervals apart and produces an exact one-direction-only polarized Nash equilibrium. Coordinating/anti-coordinating opinion games have a different dependence on others’ actions; no covering theorem was found in the inspected relevant results. This is a literature-bounded mathematical novelty assessment, not independent priority certification.
residual_risks: Shared proof architecture with the balanced two-community case: significance resides in the genuinely new asymmetric three-count phase and minimal five-person realization, not in repeating the balanced lemma.
The semantic searches and inspected primary texts do not exclude an unindexed equivalent result.
No independent historical or mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 public-goods/opinion paper highlights mixed equilibria as a central unresolved model question. The new result demonstrates that a structurally simple size imbalance permits exactly one polarity of intercommunity cooperation while both consensus states remain strict equilibria; the balanced model permits only paired polarization. The all-parameter exact census and a sharp minimal five-person witness constitute a structural phase distinction, not an arbitrary small numerical example or a parameter relabeling.
